title: Cougars vs. 'Jacks Preview: Football Matchup

Houston Football Kicks Off 2025 Season with Midweek Clash Against Stephen F. Austin The University of Houston football program begins its 80th season and third in the Big 12 Conference this Thursday,August 28th,with a 7 p.m. CT kickoff against Stephen F. Austin at TDECU Stadium.The game will be broadcast on ESPN+.
Cougars Prepare for New Season with High Expectations Head Coach Willie Fritz enters his second season at the helm with a team boasting experienced quarterbacks and a defense aiming to build on recent success.Houston (0-0, 0-0 Big 12) will look to start the season strong against the Lumberjacks (0-0, 0-0 Southland). Fans are encouraged to arrive early, with tailgating in Cougar Alley beginning at 4 p.m., followed by stadium opening at 5:30 p.m., “Coogs on Parade” at 5:50 p.m., and the Spirit of Houston taking the field at 6:45 p.m.
Gameday Experience: “Coog Fest” and More Beyond the on-field action, fans can enjoy a variety of pregame activities dubbed “Coog Fest.” A “Rodeo Round up Corral” near the Kids’ Zone will offer western-themed fun, including mini lasso practice, line dancing lessons, a belt buckle coloring station, and a mechanical bull. Fans can also enjoy live music from the band “The Tontons” on the main stage.
Offensive Outlook: Quarterback Competition and Returning Talent The quarterback position remains a key storyline, with Head Coach Fritz evaluating Donaven McCulley, Matthew Golden, and Parker Martin throughout fall camp. The Cougars return several key offensive players, including running back Stacy Sneed, who rushed for 683 yards and eight touchdowns last season.Wide receiver stephon Johnson also returns after leading the team with 69 receptions for 796 yards.
Offensive Coordinator Shannon Dawson will look to build an explosive offense that can capitalize on the team’s playmakers. Last season, Houston averaged 30.8 points per game, ranking 38th nationally.
Defensive Strategy: Aggression and Turnover Creation On the defensive side, first-year Defensive Coordinator Austin Armstrong aims to maintain the unit’s recent success. Last season, the Cougars allowed the ninth-fewest first downs nationally (214) and just 324.8 yards per game, ranking 25th nationally.Armstrong’s goal is to replicate the aggressive coverage and turnover-forcing ability he demonstrated at florida, where his defense ranked ninth in red zone defense and 13th in turnovers gained.
New Facilities and Ancient Success The team will play in front of a new backdrop this season, having recently moved into the $130 million Memorial Hermann Football Operations Center. the state-of-the-art facility includes sports performance centers, academic support suites, a leading-edge locker room, and premium seating options at TDECU stadium.
Historically, Houston has been a consistent winner, boasting 106 victories as 2011 – fourth-most in Texas behind Texas A&M, TCU, and Texas. The Cougars are 42-35-2 all-time in season openers and Head Coach Fritz has a 23-9 record in season openers throughout his career.
Scouting Stephen F. Austin Stephen F. Austin enters the 2025 season ranked #24/#23 in the major FCS preseason polls.The Lumberjacks finished the 2024 season with a 7-5 record, including victories over #22/RV Lamar and #11/#12 Abilene Christian. However, they struggled on the road, posting a 2-4 record away from home. This will be the third season under Head Coach Colby Carthel, who has a 33-35 record with the program.
Historically,Stephen F. Austin holds a 2-1 advantage in the all-time series, having won the last meeting 21-13 in 1948.
